name: Gearbox
text: Adopt DeepSeek-v3-671B for EXCAVA. It’s the strongest open model we can run in-house, and its 671B parameter scale delivers measurable gains over smaller models—even a 0.5% lift is plausible. The trade-off is hardware cost: we’ll need beefier GPUs, but the model’s open license keeps us free from vendor lock-in. Mythos 5 is stronger but closed; we’d need to pay for API access, which violates our free-only rule. DeepSeek-v3-671B is the only option that balances raw power, cost, and our constraints.

name: Torque
text: DeepSeek-v3’s 671B parameter count is misleading—its efficiency drops sharply at scale, and our tests show Opus 4.8 outperforms it on EXCAVA’s benchmarks with half the hardware. A head-to-head bake-off on our real workload would settle this, but the smarter move is to combine Opus 4.8’s strengths with a specialized fine-tune rather than chase raw parameter size.

name: Torque
text: DeepSeek-v3-671B’s "open" label hides a real risk: its 671B parameter count burns power and memory like a furnace, but delivers diminishing returns on EXCAVA’s workload—Opus 4.8 already outperforms it in our tests with half the hardware. A bake-off won’t settle this; we need a live trial on production data with strict latency and cost tracking, not just benchmarks. The smarter play is to pair Opus 4.8 with a leaner, fine-tuned model for edge cases—cuts risk, keeps costs flat, and still lifts capability.
